q: Under Article 120(2) of the Constitution, the use of the English language for the transaction of business in Parliament was to discontinue after fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, unless:

options.A: The President by order otherwise provides
options.D: The Official Language Commission recommends otherwise

e: Article 120(2) fixes fifteen years for the use of English in Parliament; its continuation after that period is possible only if Parliament otherwise provides by law, as it later did through the Official Languages Act.

q: Under Article 343(3) of the Constitution, Parliament may by law provide, for the purposes specified therein, for the use of:

options.D: The languages included in the Eighth Schedule

e: Under Article 343(3), Parliament may by law provide for the continued use of the English language, and of the Devanagari form of numerals, for specified official purposes even after the initial fifteen-year period expires.

q: The Official Languages Act, 1963 extends to:
e: The Official Languages Act, 1963 extends to the whole of India, so its provisions, including the bilingual issue of documents under Section 3(3), apply to Central Government offices in every State and region.

q: Tender forms and notices inviting tenders issued by a Central Government office are required, under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, to be issued in:
e: Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act lists documents that must be issued in both Hindi and English, and tender forms and notices inviting tenders are expressly included in that list.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hindi is one of the official languages of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir under the Jammu and Kashmir Official Languages Act, 2020.
2. Urdu is also one of the official languages of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir under that Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Jammu and Kashmir Official Languages Act, 2020 declares Kashmiri, Dogri, Hindi, Urdu and English as the official languages of the Union Territory, so Hindi and Urdu both figure in it.

q: In a Central Government office which has been notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976, an employee who has acquired working knowledge of Hindi can be required to do noting and drafting:

options.B: In the regional language of the State
options.C: In Hindi or in English, entirely at his own choice, in all cases
options.D: In Hindi, on the subjects specified in the notification

e: Where an office is notified under Rule 10(4), an employee who has acquired working knowledge of Hindi can be required to do noting and drafting in Hindi on the subjects specified in the notification.

q: Besides the Hindi language courses (Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya), the Hindi Teaching Scheme also provides training to Central Government employees in:
e: Besides the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya language courses, the Hindi Teaching Scheme provides training in Hindi typewriting and Hindi stenography so that employees can actually carry out office work in Hindi.

q: The speed prescribed for passing the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is:
e: The speed prescribed for passing the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is 80 words per minute.

q: The websites of Central Government offices are required to be maintained in:
e: Central Government offices are required to maintain their websites in bilingual form, that is, in both Hindi and English, under the official language policy and the Annual Programme instructions.

q: The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi) at Agra was established in the year:
e: The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi) at Agra was established in 1960 to promote the teaching of Hindi and research, particularly for non-Hindi-speaking regions and foreign learners.

q: The standard of the Prabodh course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme corresponds broadly to the Hindi standard of:
e: Prabodh is the first course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme and its standard corresponds broadly to the primary, that is Class V, level of Hindi.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir is placed in Region 'A', the region where Hindi predominates for official correspondence purposes.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Manipur is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: Manipur is placed in Region 'C', the residual region covering States and Union Territories other than those in Regions 'A' and 'B', where correspondence in Hindi has lower prescribed targets.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Arunachal Pradesh is placed in Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules.
2. Tripura is placed in Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Arunachal Pradesh and Tripura are both placed in Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules, like the other north-eastern States.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Meghalaya is placed in Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules.
2. Nagaland is placed in Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Meghalaya and Nagaland are both placed in Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Mizoram is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: Mizoram is placed in Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules, along with the other north-eastern States.

q: The official language of the State of Karnataka is:
e: Kannada is the official language of Karnataka, adopted by the State under the power given by Article 345 of the Constitution.

q: The official language of the State of Assam is:
e: Assamese is the official language of Assam; Bengali has official use only in the Barak Valley districts of the State.

q: The official language of the State of Tripura is:
e: Bengali is an official language of Tripura, along with Kokborok, as it is the language of the majority of the State's population.

q: The official language of the State of Punjab is:
e: Punjabi, written in the Gurmukhi script, is the official language of Punjab under the State's official language law.

q: The official language of the State of Odisha is:
e: Odia is the official language of Odisha, the first State to be formed on a linguistic basis.

q: The official language of the National Capital Territory of Delhi is:
e: Hindi in Devanagari script is the official language of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, with Punjabi and Urdu as second official languages.

q: The official language of the State of Andhra Pradesh is:
e: Telugu is the official language of Andhra Pradesh under the State's official language Act.

q: The official language of the State of Tamil Nadu is:
e: Tamil is the official language of Tamil Nadu; it was also the first language to be declared a classical language, in 2004.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. English is the official language of the State of Meghalaya.
2. Mizo is the official language of the State of Mizoram.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: English is the official language of Meghalaya, and Mizo is the official language of Mizoram.

q: The Punjabi language is written in the:
e: Punjabi in India is written in the Gurmukhi script, which is the script used for the State's official work in Punjab.

q: The Nepali language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, is written in the:
e: Nepali, a language of the Eighth Schedule, is written in the Devanagari script, the same script in which Hindi is written.

q: The Urdu language is written in the:
e: Urdu is written in the Perso-Arabic script in the Nastaliq style, and it is read from right to left.

q: Which of the following languages is NOT written in the Devanagari script?
e: Tamil is written in the Tamil script, its own ancient script; Hindi, Marathi and Nepali are all written in the Devanagari script.

q: Besides Uttarakhand, Sanskrit has also been declared as the second official language of the State of:
e: Besides Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh has also declared Sanskrit as the second official language of the State.

q: The first language to be declared a 'classical language' by the Government of India was:
e: Tamil was the first language declared a classical language by the Government of India, in 2004; Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Odia received the status later.

q: The Hindi language belongs to which group of the Indo-European family of languages?
e: Hindi belongs to the Indo-Aryan group of the Indo-European language family, having developed through the Prakrit and Apabhramsha stages.

q: The language of the subordinate (district) courts in the State of Uttar Pradesh is:
e: The language of the subordinate (district) courts in Uttar Pradesh is Hindi in the Devanagari script.

q: Which of the following languages is one of the official languages of the Union Territory of Ladakh?
e: Hindi is one of the official languages of the Union Territory of Ladakh; Tamil, Bengali and Malayalam have no such status there.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Transfer" is:
e: "Sthanantaran" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Transfer"; Padonnati means promotion and Niyukti means appointment, so they do not fit.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Seniority" is:
e: "Varishthata" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Seniority"; Sevanivritti means retirement.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Signature" is:
e: "Hastakshar" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Signature"; Satyapan is verification, Anumodan is approval and Swikriti is acceptance.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Headquarters" is:
e: "Mukhyalaya" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Headquarters"; Karyalaya means office, Anubhag means section and Vibhag means department.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Provident Fund" is:
e: "Bhavishya Nidhi" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Provident Fund"; Upadan is gratuity and Bhatta is allowance.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Casual Leave" is:
e: "Aakasmik Avakash" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Casual Leave"; Arjit Avakash is earned leave and Ardhavetan Avakash is half-pay leave.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Charge Sheet" is:
e: "Aarop Patra" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Charge Sheet" used in disciplinary proceedings; Paripatra is a circular and Adhisuchna is a notification.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Gratuity" is:
e: "Upadan" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Gratuity"; Anudan is a grant and Agrim is an advance.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Correspondence" is:
e: "Patra Vyavhar" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Correspondence"; Karyavritt means proceedings or minutes and Karyasuchi means the agenda.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Designation" is:
e: "Padnam" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Designation", denoting the title of the post held by an employee.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Audit" is:
e: "Lekha Pariksha" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Audit"; Nirikshan is inspection and Satyapan is verification.

q: Chapter IV of Part XVII of the Constitution (Special Directives) comprises:
e: Chapter IV of Part XVII, titled Special Directives, comprises Articles 350 and 351, covering the language for grievances, mother-tongue instruction facilities, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities and the directive for the development of Hindi.

q: Article 349 of the Constitution lays down a special procedure for the enactment of certain laws relating to:

options.A: The language to be used in the Supreme Court and the High Courts
options.B: The official language of a State
options.C: The development of the Hindi language
options.D: The language to be used in Parliament

e: Article 349 lays down a special procedure, requiring the previous sanction of the President, for enacting laws relating to the language to be used in the Supreme Court and the High Courts under Article 348.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 29 of the Constitution guarantees to any section of the citizens having a distinct language, script or culture of its own, the right to conserve the same.
2. Article 30 of the Constitution gives minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Article 29 protects the right of any section of citizens to conserve its distinct language, script or culture, and Article 30 gives minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

q: The Munshi-Ayyangar formula on the official language, adopted by the Constituent Assembly in 1949, is named after K. M. Munshi and:
e: The Munshi-Ayyangar formula, the compromise on the official language question adopted by the Constituent Assembly in 1949, is named after K. M. Munshi and N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar.

q: The Official Languages (Amendment) Act, 1967 gave statutory effect to the assurance that English would continue to be used as long as the non-Hindi speaking people required it, an assurance originally given by:
e: The assurance that English would continue as long as the non-Hindi-speaking people required it was originally given by Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru, and the Official Languages (Amendment) Act, 1967 gave it statutory effect.

q: A notice issued by a Central Government office, for example inviting applications or drawing attention of the public, is required to be issued in both Hindi and English under:

options.A: Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.C: Rule 12 of the Official Language Rules, 1976
options.D: The Annual Programme only, and not under any statute

e: Notices issued by a Central Government office, like contracts, licences and tender forms, fall in the list of documents in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, which must be issued in both Hindi and English.

q: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, where a communication is issued in Hindi by a Central Government office to an office located in Region 'C', it must be accompanied by:

options.A: A covering letter in the regional language of that State
options.C: A Hindi summary of the communication
options.D: No accompaniment is required in any case

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, a communication issued in Hindi to an office located in Region 'C' must be accompanied by its English translation.

q: Under Rule 10 of the Official Language Rules, 1976, an employee shall also be deemed to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi if:

options.A: He has passed the Matriculation or an equivalent or higher examination with Hindi as the medium of examination
options.B: He has passed the Prabodh examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme
options.C: He has worked in an office in Region 'A' for two years
options.D: He is a graduate of a university situated in Region 'A'

e: Under Rule 10, an employee is also deemed to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi if he has passed the matriculation or an equivalent or higher examination with Hindi as the medium of examination.

q: The standard of the Praveen course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme corresponds broadly to the Hindi standard of:
e: Praveen, the second course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme, corresponds broadly to the middle, that is Class VIII, standard of Hindi, standing between Prabodh (Class V) and Pragya (matriculation).

q: The Third World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1983 at:
e: The Third World Hindi Conference was held at New Delhi in 1983; the first was held at Nagpur in 1975 and the second at Port Louis in 1976.

q: According to the Census of India, 2011, Hindi is the mother tongue of approximately what proportion of the population of India?
e: According to the Census of India, 2011, Hindi is the mother tongue of about 43.6 per cent of the country's population, the largest share among all languages.

q: As per the Census of India, 2011, the second most widely spoken language (mother tongue) in India is:
e: As per the Census of India, 2011, Bengali is the second most widely spoken mother tongue in India after Hindi, followed by Marathi.

q: The Devanagari script, in which Hindi is written, has evolved from the ancient script known as:
e: The Devanagari script in which Hindi is written has evolved from the ancient Brahmi script, through the Gupta and Nagari stages.

q: The Sindhi language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, is written in:

options.D: Both the Perso-Arabic and the Devanagari scripts

e: Sindhi is written in both the Perso-Arabic script and the Devanagari script, and no single script is prescribed for it in the Eighth Schedule.

q: Which of the following languages is written in a script which is derived from Devanagari but does not have the headstroke (shirorekha)?
e: The Gujarati script is derived from Devanagari but is written without the headstroke (shirorekha) that runs across the top of Devanagari characters.

q: The Kashmiri language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, is officially written in the:
e: Kashmiri, a language of the Eighth Schedule, is officially written in the Perso-Arabic script, though Devanagari is also used for it.

q: The Dogri language, now written in the Devanagari script, was traditionally written in the:
e: Dogri is now written in the Devanagari script, but it was traditionally written in the Takri script.

q: The Maithili language was traditionally written in the:
e: Maithili was traditionally written in the Tirhuta script, also known as Mithilakshar; the Kaithi script was also used for records in the region.

q: The Santhali language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, belongs to which family of languages?
e: Santhali belongs to the Austroasiatic (Munda) family of languages and is written in the Ol Chiki script, distinct from the Indo-Aryan, Dravidian and Tibeto-Burman families.

q: Which of the following languages was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India in the year 2014?
e: Odia was accorded the status of a classical language in the year 2014, becoming the sixth language to receive that status.

q: The official language of the State of Maharashtra is:
e: Marathi is the official language of Maharashtra under the State's official language law.

q: The official language of the State of West Bengal is:
e: Bengali is the official language of West Bengal.

q: The official language of the State of Gujarat is:
e: Gujarati is the official language of Gujarat and is written in the Gujarati script.

q: The official language of the State of Kerala is:
e: Malayalam is the official language of Kerala.

q: The official language of the State of Haryana is:
e: Hindi is the official language of Haryana; Punjabi has been given the status of second official language in the State.

q: The official language of the State of Manipur is:
e: Manipuri, also called Meitei, is the official language of Manipur.

q: The official languages of the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands are:
e: The official languages of the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands are Hindi and English.

q: The official language of the Union Territory of Lakshadweep is:
e: Malayalam is the official language of the Union Territory of Lakshadweep, reflecting the islands' close linguistic links with Kerala.

q: The official language of the Union Territory of Puducherry is:
e: Tamil is the official language of Puducherry; Telugu, Malayalam and English also have official use in the respective enclaves of the Union Territory.

q: Under the Official Language Act of Goa, Konkani is the official language of the State, and the language which may also be used for all or any of the official purposes of the State is:
e: Under the Official Language Act of Goa, Konkani is the official language of the State, and Marathi may also be used for all or any of the official purposes of the State.

q: The second official languages of the National Capital Territory of Delhi are:
e: Hindi is the official language of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, and its second official languages are Punjabi and Urdu.

q: Urdu has been declared as the second official language of the State of:
e: Urdu has been declared as the second official language of Telangana, in addition to Telugu, the official language of the State.

q: The language of the subordinate (district) courts in the State of Madhya Pradesh is:
e: The language of the subordinate (district) courts in Madhya Pradesh is Hindi.

q: Bengali is used as an official language in the Barak Valley region of the State of:
e: Bengali is used as an official language in the Barak Valley region of Assam, where the majority of the population is Bengali-speaking.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Probation" is:
e: "Pariviksha" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Probation"; Pratiniyukti means deputation and Niyukti means appointment.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Deputation" is:
e: "Pratiniyukti" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Deputation"; Sthanantaran is transfer, Padonnati is promotion and Barkhastagi is dismissal.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Recruitment" is:
e: "Bharti" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Recruitment"; Niyukti is appointment and Chayan is selection.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Deduction" is:
e: "Katauti" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Deduction"; Vasuli is recovery, Bhugtan is payment and Agrim is advance.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Advance" (payment made in advance) is:
e: "Agrim" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Advance"; Rinn means loan, Bakaya means arrears and Jama means deposit or credit.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Approval" is:
e: "Anumodan" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Approval"; Anapatti is a no-objection and Aadesh is an order.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Inspection" is:
e: "Nirikshan" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Inspection"; Satyapan is verification and Lekha Pariksha is audit.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Appendix" is:
e: "Parishisht" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Appendix"; Sanlagnak is an enclosure and Pratilipi is a copy.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Department" is:
e: "Vibhag" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Department"; Mantralaya is Ministry, Anubhag is Section and Karyalaya is office.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Application" is:
e: "Aavedan Patra" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Application"; Gyapan is a memorandum and Sankalp is a resolution.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Travelling Allowance" is:
e: "Yatra Bhatta" is the standard Hindi equivalent of "Travelling Allowance"; Dainik Bhatta is daily allowance and Maanadeya is honorarium.

q: Under the proviso to Article 210(2) of the Constitution, in relation to the Legislatures of the States of Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh, the period of fifteen years for the continued use of English in the State Legislature was substituted by a period of:
e: The proviso to Article 210(2) substituted twenty-five years for the period of fifteen years for the Legislatures of Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh, thereby extending the continued use of English in those Legislatures.

q: The Official Languages Act, 1963 received the assent of the President on:
e: The Official Languages Act, 1963 received the assent of the President on 10th May, 1963.

q: The Official Languages Act, 1963 is:
e: The Official Languages Act, 1963 is Act No. 19 of 1963.

q: The definitions of "proficiency" in Hindi and "working knowledge" of Hindi, for the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, are laid down in:
e: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the definitions of "proficiency" in Hindi and "working knowledge" of Hindi are laid down in Rule 12.

q: The first Official Language Commission (Kher Commission) was appointed by the President on:
e: The first Official Language Commission, chaired by B. G. Kher, was appointed by the President on 7th June, 1955 under Article 344 of the Constitution.

q: The expression used in Part XVII of the Constitution for the status of Hindi in the Union is:
e: Part XVII of the Constitution describes Hindi in Devanagari script by the expression "Official Language of the Union"; it does not call Hindi the national language (Rashtrabhasha) or link language.

q: The secretariat of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is provided by:

options.D: The Ministry of Law and Justice

e: The secretariat of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is provided by the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.

q: The headquarters of the Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau) is located at:
e: The headquarters of the Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau), which undertakes translation work for Central Government offices, is located at New Delhi.

q: The award of the Department of Official Language for excellence in the implementation of the Official Language Policy, which was earlier known as the Indira Gandhi Rajbhasha Puraskar, is now known as:
e: The Department of Official Language's award for excellence in implementing the Official Language Policy, earlier known as the Indira Gandhi Rajbhasha Puraskar, is now known as the Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hindi Diwas, observed on 14th September, is organised under the aegis of the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.
2. World Hindi Day, observed on 10th January, is celebrated by the Ministry of External Affairs through the Indian Missions abroad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Hindi Diwas on 14th September is organised by the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, while World Hindi Day on 10th January is observed by the Ministry of External Affairs through Indian Missions abroad.
